clue.text: Bone in fish — meal putting me off

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: putting, with off, says the word me is put off, dropped from meal
off says the word me is dropped from meal

explanation.surface: A recipe gripe: a fish bone in the dish has put the diner off the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting me off' strips ME from MEAL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpal is any of the small wrist bones, so the noun works as a bone.

clue.text: Sound coming through the mouth? Through the ear!

indicators.note: Sound, read as a verb, says the following words must be heard, not read

parts.note: spoken by mouth, oral

explanation.surface: A sharp correction: a sound does not come through the mouth, it comes through the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the signal: ORAL said aloud gives AURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural means relating to hearing, perceived by the ear.

clue.text: Power one observed in catty type leading a new church

indicators.note: leading puts the cat piece in front of what follows
observed in places the numeral within the cat's name

parts.note: a puss is a cat
one is the Roman numeral I
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A spiteful character's authority grows as they head a newly founded church.
explanation.definitionFit: Puissance is an old word for might or strength, also a show-jumping test of power.

clue.text: Boy's story probed by a theologian

indicators.note: probed by puts the following pieces inside the story word

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: A boy's tale is questioned by a learned theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddie is a Scottish, affectionate word for a young lad.

clue.text: Country singer returned offering a few notes maybe

parts.note: Johnny Cash, the American country singer
back means returned, as in came back

explanation.surface: A country singer comes back with a few musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The notes are banknotes, not music: shops in the UK hand cash out at the till as cashback.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashback is money taken in banknotes at a shop till alongside a card purchase.

clue.text: Heads condemning wrong decided on a new course of action?

definitions.text: decided on a new course of action?

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of the preceding words are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Leaders who condemned a wrong have reversed their policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' looks like the thing condemned; it is the signal to rearrange HEADS CONDEMNING.
explanation.definitionFit: To change one's mind is the idiom for reaching a different decision.

clue.text: Unhealthy group erred, from what we hear and see

indicators.note: from what we hear says the preceding word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to have erred morally is to have sinned
the Holy See is in Rome

explanation.surface: A sickly gang went astray, as far as one can hear and see.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNED spoken gives SYND; the See is the Pope's seat, Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a cluster of symptoms that together mark a disorder.

clue.text: Something indistinct and black that may be on book's cover

definitions.text: that may be on book's cover

parts.note: a blur is a shape seen unclearly
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark smudge mars a book jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the promotional text printed on a book's jacket.

clue.text: Deliverer of goods tricks uninformed worker needing dispatch

parts.note: cons are swindles or tricks

indicators.note: dispatch means getting rid of, so the worker is removed from uninformed

parts.note: uninformed means ignorant
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A courier cheats an ignorant employee who needs sending off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatch' sounds like part of delivery; it signals taking ANT out of IGNORANT to leave IGNOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignor is the party who sends goods off to a recipient.

clue.text: A reason for empty chairs in our country?

definitions.text: A reason for empty chairs in our country?

parts.words: A reason for empty chairs in our country?
parts.note: chairs are university professorships, left vacant when academics emigrate

explanation.surface: Why are there empty seats around the country?
explanation.walkthrough: 'chairs' suggests furniture; it means professorial posts, emptied by skilled people leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the emigration of highly educated people, leaving academic posts unfilled.

clue.text: Scottish poet, not the first, to make pots

indicators.note: not the first says the poet's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Robert Burns, Scotland's national poet

explanation.surface: A beheaded Robert Burns makes pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are large vases or pots, often for ashes.

clue.text: Strip of metal or wood to chuck outside

indicators.note: outside puts the throwing word around the wood

parts.note: to fling is to chuck or throw
ash is a timber tree

explanation.surface: Choosing between metal and wood, someone chucks the strip outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or wood' reads as offering a choice of material, but wood here is a tree's timber, and 'outside' tells the throwing word to wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashing is the sheet metal sealing roof joints against water.

clue.text: Game with helpful person endlessly offering set of rules

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a brick is a reliable, helpful person

explanation.surface: A sport with a kindly volunteer provides the rulebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubric is a set of instructions or rules, as on an exam paper.

clue.text: Bridge partner of North facing censure

indicators.note: facing puts the partner in front of the censure

parts.note: in the card game bridge, North partners South, S
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A bridge player's partner faces criticism at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game; it is the definition, a span crossing a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the stretch of a bridge between supports, or the bridge itself.

clue.text: You'd want me in an emergency? I'd let you down!

definitions.text: You'd want me in an emergency? I'd let you down!

parts.words: You'd want me in an emergency? I'd let you down!
parts.note: a skydiver's canopy lowers you gently; letting down sounds like failure

explanation.surface: An unreliable helper boasts of being needed then failing you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let you down' means disappoint, but here it means lower you safely to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy device that slows a fall, used when bailing out of an aircraft.

clue.text: It's certainly not helping mother, getting old

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
aging means getting old

explanation.surface: Mum growing older is no help at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaging causes harm, the opposite of helping.

clue.text: One fellow helping another at an American match

definitions.text: One fellow helping another at an American match

parts.words: One fellow helping another at an American match
parts.note: a match is a marriage; a man attending the bridegroom at a US wedding

explanation.surface: A man assisting a teammate at a US sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport; it is a wedding, where one man helps another, the bridegroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The American term for an usher or attendant supporting the bridegroom at a wedding.

clue.text: Cleric involved in secret sin immediately shown up

indicators.note: shown up says the hidden letters are read backwards
involved in says the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clergyman's hidden sin is exposed at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'involved' in the definition; 'involved in' is the signal that the letters lie inside the words, and in a down clue 'shown up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

clue.text: Asian fellows taken in by heretic

indicators.note: taken in by puts the fellows inside the heretic

parts.note: an Arian followed the heresy of Arius
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Some Asian men are fooled by a heretic.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia lies in western Asia, so its people are Asian.

clue.text: Plant knocked over in dark office

indicators.note: knocked over says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pot plant gets knocked over in an unlit office.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no signal for the hiding; 'in' is it.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a plant grown for its edible green pods, also called ladies' fingers.

clue.text: Single old females escape for adventure perhaps

parts.note: a single in cricket is one run
F is female; FF is females

explanation.surface: Unmarried elderly women break away for some excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' suggests unmarried; it is a cricket single, one RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off is to leave suddenly, as eloping lovers or adventurers do.

clue.text: Trick needed with very good sea food

parts.note: a scam is a trick or swindle
PI, short for pious, means very good

explanation.surface: A con needs some fine seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, a classic battered seafood dish.

clue.text: Maureen is on phone — somewhere for overnight stay needed

parts.note: Mo is a short form of Maureen
TEL is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: Maureen is on the phone, needing a room for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a roadside hotel where motorists stop for the night.

clue.text: Close friend — solitary, it's said, facing position of defeat

indicators.note: facing puts the first piece in front of the second
it's said says the preceding word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sole means single or solitary
mate in chess is the losing position

explanation.surface: A lonely chess player faces checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A soulmate is someone deeply understood and close, an ideal partner.

clue.text: Fusses, there being a list of upcoming jobs?

definitions.meaning: tasks still to be done, written as items on a list

explanation.surface: Complaining about a long schedule of chores.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both fusses and outstanding tasks on a list.

clue.text: Pollution maybe from industry

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the next word

explanation.surface: Some pollution coming from industrial works.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne particles are one example of pollution, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Odd bits of old material specially fashioned for customer

indicators.note: specially, as in specially arranged, says the letters are put in a new order
odd bits of takes the first and third letters of the short word old

explanation.surface: Offcuts of old fabric made up specially for a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd bits of' looks like scraps of cloth; it picks OD from old. 'specially' then rearranges OD plus MATERIAL. 'specially fashioned' wants to be one phrase, but 'specially' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing made to measure is cut and sewn to suit one particular client.

clue.text: We will be not half embarrassed and polite

parts.note: we'll is the contraction of we will

indicators.note: not half says only one half of the short word is kept

parts.note: to be red in the face is to be embarrassed

explanation.surface: We'll be slightly flustered yet courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' reads as slang for 'very'; it halves BE to B.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-bred has good manners from a refined upbringing.

clue.text: Polish or north European language being heard

indicators.note: being heard says the language name is taken by its sound

parts.note: the language of Finland

explanation.surface: Choosing between Polish and a northern European tongue in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a language; it is the verb, to finish off a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is the final polish or coating given to a surface.
